request.prompt:
Draw a PRODUCTION 12-CEL ANIMATION SHEET of this cyan/gold arcane ground effect uncoiling, splitting and dissolving. EXACT six columns and two rows, 3072x1024 PNG, each cel512x512. True transparent alpha, no text, no numbered labels, no grid, no background, no floor or furnace. Orthographic circular TOP-DOWN ground plane, same fixed center(256,256) and camera scale in all cels.

REFERENCE1 is a strict layout guide. Replace its circle regions with the animation, preserving centers and circular extents; REMOVE all guide lines/crosses/text/background in the final output. Reference2 is the mature starting pose/design. Reference3 is a motion study showing real shape changes and splitting; it is not the final animation. Retain the four muted cyan and three old gold curved hooked strips, dark tapered contour, sparse bright inner brushstrokes, little icy diamonds and purple hollow marks. Don't copy its faint background haze.

Animate EACH INDIVIDUAL STRIP advancing clockwise and outward, stretching unevenly and opening cracks, then turning into slender curling fragments and vanishing. A strip's head leads, its middle elongates and narrows, trailing tip curls and forks with a lag, and its inner highlight bends and splits along the changing shape. The whole image must NEVER scale or rotate as one object. The ring NEVER shrinks toward the center. Don't just reduce opacity of a fixed pose. Draw the changing topology of each shape.

Cel1: intact mature starting pose, matching reference2 at radius220 inside the guide, no cracks.
Cel2: heads move a few pixels clockwise/outward, tails curl slightly inward, thin notches begin at bends. Curvature changes.
Cel3: weak middles stretch thinner; two gold and two cyan strips develop open transparent cracks, interior highlights split.
Cel4: gaps lengthen; other strips crack at slightly different times. Original heads become longer and thinner, tails turn and hook.
Cel5: each long strip divides into two or three unequal curved pieces with visible gaps. No static intact arcs simply translated.
Cel6: large heads become sweeping narrow splinters, tail pieces curl like commas. Painted area falls to about55% of cel1. The circumference is slightly farther out, not smaller.
Cel7: individual fragments continue to turn and bend outward, thin ends taper away; hollow marks open at a corner and diamonds split into two pointed slivers. No new pieces arise inside.
Cel8: only curved skinny fragments remain, about30% original area. Twisting tips have different contours from cel7.
Cel9: about15% original area as short thin cyan/gold curls and a few tiny icy chips, still distributed near the outer circumference.
Cel10: about6% original area as separated slender curved dashes. No broad blades, no complete glyphs or diamonds.
Cel11: only a handful of very small tapered colored remnants at the OUTER edge, no central cluster. Each remnant follows its preceding fragment's spiral path.
Cel12: fully empty transparent cel, animation has ended.

All12 cels must maintain fixed registration and scale. The outermost visible bits fit INSIDE the guide circles: radius220 at first, gradually about238 by the end, always clear of cell borders. There is no shrinking. Render each cel as a genuinely new drawing: topology, curvature, width, tail forks, highlights and cracks change continuously. No affine-transformed copies, no random unrelated poses, no uniform-fade-only effect. Keep natural continuous motion between neighbors, repeated cyan/gold identity, clear handmade ink contour and color planes. No smoke, fire, flowers, extra decorative circles or glow clouds.
